clue.text: TV chairperson so distorted Guardian's position?

indicators.note: something distorted has been twisted out of its original shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A television presenter or panel chair warps the stance taken by the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' suggests the newspaper, but here it means a legal guardian or conservator appointed to look after someone's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatorship is the legal office of someone appointed to manage another person's property, so it is literally a guardian's post.

clue.text: Round gift cleric replaced is writer's accessory?

indicators.note: when things are replaced they are put back in a different arrangement, so the preceding letters are reordered

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A present for the vicar, swapped in a round of gift-giving, turns out to be stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: Correcting fluid (Tippex in Britain) is the white liquid painted over typing or handwriting mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers once kept a bottle of the white liquid at hand for covering errors, so it is a typical piece of desk kit.

clue.text: Enthusiast given award after turning out Dutch dish with ground food

indicators.note: turning someone out means evicting them, so a letter is expelled from the prize word

blocks.note: a nut is a fan, as in a fitness nut
a medal is an award
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A keen fan wins a prize after ordering a Dutch dish made with ground ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the reduced prize after the fan; 'Dutch dish' looks like one phrase but the Dutch letter is simply removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeal is a meal made from finely ground nuts, so it is a preparation of milled food.

clue.text: Pursue aid for renovating old theatre site

indicators.note: renovating a building means reworking it, so the preceding letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone chases funding to restore a historic theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Epidaurus in Greece has one of the best-preserved ancient Greek theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city is famed for its fourth-century BC amphitheatre, still used for performances, so it is a classical stage location.

clue.text: Rate multinational group facilities on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, something on the rise is read from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the European Union
lav is short for lavatory; 'the facilities' is a euphemism for the toilet

explanation.surface: Someone assesses an international body's amenities as they improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to judge its worth, which is what valuing it means as a verb.

clue.text: Unsettled workers' group split about leaders of business using labour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for split is wrapped round the other letters
the leaders of words are their front letters, so only the initials are kept

blocks.note: TU is a trade union
rent means torn, split apart
first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A union is divided over bosses who rely on hired workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials go inside RENT, giving R-BUL-ENT after the union letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent means disturbed or in turmoil, a close synonym of unsettled as an adjective.

clue.text: Artist snubbed leading member of a religious movement

indicators.note: a snub nose is a short one, so the next word has its end cut off

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
a star role is a leading one

explanation.surface: A painter is cold-shouldered by a prominent figure in a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist snubbed' reads as one phrase, but snubbed acts on the following word, leading.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta is a follower of Rastafarianism, the Jamaican religious movement.

clue.text: Animated liberal in Spain for high-level communication

blocks.note: hot means heated, excited
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A lively progressive in Spain sets up talks with the top brass.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a direct link between heads of government, such as Washington and Moscow, so it is top-level contact.

clue.text: Engineer finalises promos showing fitting competence

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the following letters are built into something new

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A sound engineer completes promotional tracks and proves suitably capable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a noun for a person but is a verb instructing the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionalism is the skill and conduct appropriate to an expert, so it is suitable, proper ability.

clue.text: Another hearing about natural walk slightly altered

indicators.note: slightly altered says the word is changed a little, here by swapping a couple of letters

blocks.note: re means concerning
a nature trail is a walk through the countryside

explanation.surface: A second court session concerns a country path that has been changed a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a case heard in court again, a second hearing of the same matter.

clue.text: Trio's prepared starters of Tuscan olives — or other dish?

indicators.note: something prepared in the kitchen has been worked on, so these letters are rearranged
starters are what come first, so only the initial letters are taken

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
initial letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Three cooks serve an antipasto of Tuscan olives, or some other course?
explanation.walkthrough: The menu setting makes 'starters' look like appetisers; here they are first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock, a classic plate of food.

clue.text: Female recalled among urban electors

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the words that follow
recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the backward direction

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A woman is remembered by voters in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Elena is a girl's name, so it is a woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Illuminating director cutting musical prompt on return

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so one letter is inserted
on return means going back, so the musical and prompt are read backwards

blocks.note: the Lloyd Webber musical
a cue prompts an actor
D is short for director

explanation.surface: An enlightening director trims a stage show's prompt when it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The show and the prompt are reversed together first; then the director's letter cuts in after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something educative teaches and enlightens, so it is illuminating in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Hallmark of a liberal society upsetting to cleaner

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and scatters it, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A defining value of a free society proves distressing for the cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptance of differing views and lifestyles is a defining trait of an open, permissive society.

clue.text: Man on board heard by junior reporter around large social venue

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the chess piece, not its spelling
around means encircling, so the reporter goes round the size letter

blocks.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the board
a cub reporter is a trainee journalist
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A chess piece is overheard by a trainee journalist near a big gathering place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a ship's crew; it is a chess piece. The junior reporter wraps round the size letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is an entertainment venue for dancing and drinking late at night, a place for socialising.

clue.text: Teams in pleasure trip, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, so the answer matches the sound of the trip word

blocks.note: a cruise is a holiday voyage

explanation.surface: Groups of people go on a holiday voyage, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Crews are groups working together, such as rowing or ship's crews, so they are teams.

clue.text: Councillor has current woman at work as point of reference

blocks.note: Cr is the abbreviation for Councillor
I is the physics symbol for electric current
Teri is a woman's name
on means operating, on duty

explanation.surface: A council member has a female employee who serves as a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard by which things are judged, a fixed point to measure against.

clue.text: Name house in retreat in French city

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the house word is read from right to left

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: Someone names a holiday home where they retreat in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi, a semi-detached house, shares one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimes is a city in southern France known for its Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: This person's flipping left to go up as ex- Health Secretary

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the self-reference is written back to front

blocks.note: the setter says I'm, I am
L is the abbreviation for left
to go up in flames is to burn

explanation.surface: The speaker is flip-flopping on whether to leave as a former minister rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' is the setter speaking: this person is = I'm. To go up is to go up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Milburn was the UK Labour government's Secretary of State for Health from 1999 to 2003.

clue.text: Become aware of European in tangle beset by awful ego

indicators.note: in says one letter sits inside the word for tangle
beset by means surrounded on all sides, so the outer letters enclose everything else
awful means dreadful or messed up, so the letters of the next word are disordered

blocks.note: the three letters of ego in another order
a twist is a tangle
E is short for European

explanation.surface: A European caught up in a mess is surrounded by a terrible ego and finally catches on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' means surrounded by: the European goes into the tangle, and the reshuffled ego wraps round the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To get wise to something is an informal idiom for coming to realise or discover it.

clue.text: Use up quantity of money in worry over round

indicators.note: in says the money word is placed inside the word for worry

blocks.note: what's eating you means what's worrying you
tin is slang for money
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone spends a sum fretting about a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the earlier part on top of the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings or time is to consume part of them, so it is an idiom for using up.

clue.text: Stumble to find pest, as it were

blocks.note: first meaning: a trip or misstep
second meaning, cryptic: the word pest is what you get from a wrong arrangement of a four-letter word for a pace

explanation.walkthrough: PEST is STEP with its letters falsified, so a pest is, as it were, a false step. 'as it were' flags the whimsical second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A false step is literally a misplaced foot causing a trip, and figuratively a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Avoid fool lacking in degree

indicators.note: lacking in means missing, so a letter is dropped from the fool word

blocks.note: to delude is to fool
D is short for degree

explanation.surface: Steer clear of an idiot who is short of a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' looks like a noun for an idiot but is the verb to trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude someone is to evade or escape them, which is avoiding them.

clue.text: Character found at front of punishing race, possibly

definitions.text: Character found at front of punishing race, possibly

indicators.note: the character found at the front of a word is its first letter
possibly suggests one of several versions, so the letters of the word before it can be reordered

blocks.note: first letter of this word
the four letters of race in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted leading the field in a gruelling contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a pacer runs at the front to set a demanding speed in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer or pacemaker is a runner who leads early in a race to set a fast tempo for others.

clue.text: Section in text rattled one at the rear of scene?

definitions.text: one at the rear of scene?

indicators.note: a section in a passage is a portion of it, so the letters are lifted from inside the words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A passage in a script unnerved the bit-part actor at the back of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer sits there in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is a non-speaking performer in the background of a shot, at the back of the scene.

clue.text: A French bun's durable regularly? No, that's rare

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: un is the French for a
the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: Is a French bread roll always long-lasting? No, that would be uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual is out of the ordinary, which is what rare means as an adjective.

clue.text: Rallying call to tour island, one producing Italian tipple

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so the call wraps around the island letter

blocks.note: a chant is a crowd's rallying cry
I is short for island
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cry from supporters on an island tour leads someone to make Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so it is an Italian drink.

clue.text: Abominable diner disturbed noted figure guiding players?

indicators.note: something disturbed has been thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A dreadful restaurant customer is upset, perhaps a famous team coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' hints at musical notes; the players are orchestral musicians, not a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Barenboim is a famous conductor, who directs orchestral musicians from the podium.
